raw_response:
I’m 66 this year, and I’ve farmed this land a long time, so I don’t like making big changes unless there is a clear reason. On my 12 mu, I’ll still keep the familiar pattern: most of the land in wheat-maize double cropping, and a smaller piece in cotton. Wheat and maize are still my steady income, and cotton gives me another channel in case grain price is not good. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I can’t make the management too complicated. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I’ll irrigate at the key stages, not blindly.

For wheat, I’ll put more attention on base fertilizer and one topdressing at jointing, because that has worked reliably for me. I usually don’t dare cut nitrogen too much, since if wheat turns weak in spring, yield drops fast. After wheat harvest, maize has to go in quickly, so I’ll keep the turnaround simple, with light residue handling and direct sowing or quick rotary tillage. For cotton, I won’t put too much area because it takes more watching and more spraying, but I’ll keep a few mu since I know how to manage it and it helps spread risk. I’ll use round, practical rates, roughly what I’ve seen work on my own fields and in the village, not some fancy formula.
